articleBlocks: Warning and Street make signs feel likely almost immediately, but they can also trap you in a too-literal road-and-safety reading. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Equal gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.
Peace helps widen the board, though the cleanest shift comes when one clue proves the category includes symbols and notation too.
Equal is the clue that does that work.
Once equal sign appears, the answer stops being about posted signage alone and becomes the broader category of signs.
That makes warning sign, street sign, vital signs, and peace sign all fit comfortably under the same label.
The answer was Types of signs.
This board is simple on purpose, but it still works because the clues stretch the word sign across medicine, culture, public space, and math.
solutionNarrative: Warning and Street made sign feel likely quickly, but at first I read the board too narrowly as public or cautionary signage. Vital and Peace helped, yet I still wanted one clue that proved the category was broader than that.

Equal gave me that proof. Once equal sign appeared, the board expanded into the broader idea of signs, and the earlier clues all fit more cleanly without being trapped inside road or warning contexts.
